chunks: What Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillah narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillah عليه السلام: May a man recite in his salat (prayer) while his garment is over his mouth? He said: There is no harm in that, if he can hear the murmuring.

key_terms.الْهَمْهَمَةَ: the low murmur or subdued sound of recitation that can be heard
key_terms.ثَوْبُهُ: his garment, used here as something covering the mouth
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.فِيهِ: his mouth, the place being covered during recitation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite in salat (prayer) while covering the mouth with a garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about reciting in salat (prayer) while the mouth is covered with a garment. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no problem with it, provided that the reciter can hear the low sound of his own recitation.
